M monotonically increasing in B at fixed T

M decreases with increasing T at fixed B (Curie-like)
M finite and real over the whole sampled region

role_corrections: M: output->dependent variable (confirmed; LHS quantity the equation determines)
B: V->V (confirmed independent axis: applied field)
mu: V->P (overridden: magnetic moment per site is a fixed physical constant, not a sampling axis)
lambda_W: P->P (confirmed, small paramagnetic Weiss coupling)
rationale: analyze_expression shows no derivatives or integral kernels and that the relation is explicitly solvable for M, so this is a static explicit equation evaluated pointwise (evaluate_explicit). M is the dependent variable; the phenomenon models magnetization as a function of field and temperature, so B and T are the sampling axes while mu (moment per site) and all other free symbols are fixed physical constants/parameters. Scaled natural units (kB=mu=N=1) keep the Brillouin argument mu*B/(kB*T) in the range ~0.02-10 so the data spans the linear-response regime through near-saturation. Values (J_spin=2, lambda_W=0.1, C_schottky=0.5, Delta_cf=2, chi_vv_amp=0.05, lambda_dip=0.05 mid the suggested 1e-3..1e-1) keep the Schottky reduction factor positive (~0.9-0.98) and every additive term above 5*sigma; the B start is 0.1 (not 0) to avoid the coth(0) singularity in the Brillouin combination."

scenario_text: In a paramagnetic insulator, the magnetization responds to an applied external magnetic field at fixed temperature. Independent samples are prepared and the equilibrium magnetization is recorded for various field strengths and temperatures. At strong fields the alignment of magnetic moments approaches complete saturation. The task is to model the equilibrium magnetization as a function of field and temperature.
